sentences.text: Counsel for Applicant :- Satyendra Kumar Singh Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A,Pankaj Pandey Hon'ble Vipin Chandra Dixit,J.
List has been revised.
No one is present on behalf of opposite party no.2.
Supplementary affidavit has been filed by learned counsel for the applicants, which is taken on record.
Heard learned counsel for the applicants, learned AGA for the State and perused the record.

It is submitted by learned counsel for applicants that it is a matrimonial dispute between the parties and parties had settled their dispute amicably outside the Court and a written compromise has taken place between the parties on 22.3.2023.

Copy of compromise is annexed as Annexure S.A.-1 to Niranjan Singh And 2 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on 18 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/42857936/
1 the supplementary affidavit filed today.

entities.text: Niranjan Singh And 2 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Both the parties were appeared before the court concerned on 22.3.2023, who were identified by their respective counsels and the compromise was verified by the Civil Judge (J.D.)/F.T.C.-2,
Muzaffarnagar vide order dated 22.3.2023.
Certified copy of order dated 22.3.2023 is annexed as Annexure S.A.-1 to the supplementary affidavit filed today.
Learned AGA for the State does not dispute the aforesaid facts.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of State of Madhya Pradesh Vs. Laxmi Narayan and others,
reported in (2019) 5 SCC 688 has laid down principles for quashing the proceeding on the basis of settlement/compromise.

entities.text:
State of Madhya Pradesh Vs. Laxmi Narayan and others,
reported in (2019) 5 SCC 688
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Relevant paragraph no.15 is quoted hereinbelow:-
"15.
However, the High Court would not rest its decision merely because there is a mention of Section 307 IPC in the FIR or the charge is framed under this provision.

It would be open to the High Court to examine as to whether incorporation of Section 307 IPC is there for the sake of it or the prosecution has collected sufficient evidence, which if proved, would lead to framing the charge under Section 307 IPC.

For this purpose, it would be open to the High Court to go by the nature of injury Niranjan Singh And 2 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on 18 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/42857936/
2 sustained, whether such injury is inflicted on the vital/delegate parts of the body,
nature of weapons used etc.

entities.text: Niranjan Singh And 2 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, such an exercise by the High Court would be permissible only after the evidence is collected after investigation and the charge sheet is filed/charge is framed and/or during the trial.
Such exercise is not permissible when the matter is still under investigation.

In view of the aforesaid fact, since the parties have amicably settled their dispute outside the Court and compromise between the parties had already been verified by the Court below, the present application U/s 482 Cr.P.C. is liable to be allowed.

Accordingly, the present application U/s 482 Cr.P.C. is allowed and the proceedings of Complaint Case No.453 of 2020, (Smt. Ravita Vs. Pushpendra and others), under Sections 498A, 323, 506 I.P.C. and Section 4 D.P. Act, P.S. Mahila Thana, Muzaffarnagar, is hereby quashed.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of State of Madhya Pradesh Vs. Laxmi Narayan and others,
reported in (2019) 5 SCC 688 has laid down principles for quashing the proceeding on the basis of settlement/compromise.
However, the High Court would not rest its decision merely because there is a mention of Section 307 IPC in the FIR or the charge is framed under this provision.
It would be open to the High Court to examine as to whether incorporation of Section 307 IPC is there for the sake of it or the prosecution has collected sufficient evidence, which if proved, would lead to framing the charge under Section 307 IPC.
